original_question: What happens when the amplitude of the wobbling mode in a rapidly rotating nucleus grows beyond the small-amplitude regime and the uniformly rotating nucleus becomes unstable with respect to that collective rotational degree of freedom, and how can microscopic large-amplitude collective-motion theory be applied to that regime as well as to chiral vibrations connecting right-handed and left-handed triaxial configurations?
target_in_paper: “It is an interesting open problem to explore what will happen when the amplitude of the wobbling mode increases and the uniformly rotating nucleus becomes unstable against this collective rotational degree of freedom [68,69]. … In a transient situation, where the barrier separating the two HFB solutions is still in an early stage of development, the large-amplitude vibrations connecting the two configurations, called chiral vibrations, may occur [16,70,71]. It remains for the future to apply the microscopic LACM theory to these phenomena unique to rapidly rotating nuclei with triaxial shape.”
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies (i) the growth of the wobbling mode amplitude beyond the small-amplitude (RPA) regime, (ii) the resulting instability of uniform rotation with respect to the wobbling degree of freedom, (iii) the large-amplitude chiral vibrations connecting right- and left-handed triaxial configurations, and (iv) the call for applying microscopic large-amplitude collective-motion (LACM) theory to both phenomena.
missing_details: Definition of the wobbling mode as a small-amplitude boson-like excitation built on the yrast line in triaxially deformed, rapidly rotating cold nuclei
Specification that the instability refers to a breakdown of uniform cranking rotation in the collective coordinate
Identification of the Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov (HFB) mean-field framework and the nature of the two degenerate chiral HFB solutions
Clarification that microscopic LACM theory refers to methods such as the adiabatic self-consistent collective coordinate (ASCC) approach
Quantification of the regime: beyond RPA/QRPA validity into anharmonic, large-amplitude motion
refined_question: In triaxially deformed cold nuclei near the yrast line at high angular momentum, the wobbling mode—describable as a boson-like small-amplitude vibration of the rotating mean field—exhibits significant anharmonicity in observed double-excitation bands. What is the dynamical behavior of this wobbling mode as its amplitude grows beyond the random-phase approximation regime, ultimately leading to an instability of the uniformly rotating HFB solution with respect to this collective rotational degree of freedom? Furthermore, how can the microscopic large-amplitude collective-motion theory (e.g., the adiabatic self-consistent collective coordinate method) be formulated and applied to describe both (a) the nonlinear evolution from small- to large-amplitude wobbling and the onset of rotational instability, and (b) the large-amplitude chiral vibrations connecting the right- and left-handed triaxial HFB configurations?
justification: The refined question reproduces the open problem as stated in section 7.2 of the paper, explicitly naming the wobbling mode, the breakdown of uniform rotation, the HFB mean-field context, and the application of microscopic LACM theory to both wobbling and chiral vibrations, making it self-contained and faithful to the original intent.
